alt: A grid of the three functions. Serving the economy works through skills and role allocation; social mobility through qualifications and meritocracy; social cohesion through shared norms and values. Rows give an example of each, then the Marxist and feminist judgement, such as the myth of meritocracy and the glass ceiling.
caption: For each function, show how it works and how each perspective judges it.

alt: Five cards set out Durkheim’s ideas: education welds individuals into a united whole, history links individuals to society, school teaches cooperation with non-kin, strict rules teach self-discipline, and the school is a society in miniature. A sixth card gives evaluation: ruling-class norms, diverse societies, and pupils such as Willis’s lads rejecting school values.
caption: For Durkheim, school turns a mass of individuals into a united whole.

alt: Two panels. Durkheim emphasises cohesion, moral discipline and the school as society in miniature. Parsons emphasises meritocracy, achieved status, selection and the school as a bridge to universalistic standards. Below, two criticisms quoted in the specification.
caption: Cohesion and discipline: Durkheim. Meritocracy and universalistic standards: Parsons.

alt: Primary schools take ages 4 or 5 to 11 and secondary schools 11 to 16 or 18. State-funded schools are free and include community schools, academies and free schools, selective grammar schools and faith schools. Private schools are fee-paying and need not follow the National Curriculum; Marxists say they reproduce elite advantage.
caption: Sort schools by age, then by who funds and controls them.

alt: Two panels. Home schooling is legal in England and keeps a planned education outside school, chosen for reasons such as bullying or beliefs, and depends on parents’ resources. De-schooling, from Illich, rejects schools, which he said teach pupils to confuse being taught with learning, and proposes learning webs.
caption: Home schooling moves education out of school; de-schooling rejects school itself.
